faqs.a: BMR is what you burn at complete rest, keeping your organs running. TDEE adds everything else: work, walking, exercise and fidgeting. You lose weight by eating below TDEE, not below BMR.
faqs.q: What is the difference between BMR and TDEE?

faqs.q: How accurate is the Mifflin-St Jeor formula?

faqs.q: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?

faqs.a: BMR falls as you lose weight, because a smaller body costs less to run. That is why plateaus happen and why calorie targets need recalculating every few kilograms.
faqs.q: Why does my BMR drop when I lose weight?

bmr-calculator.formula:
Mifflin-St Jeor:
Male: BMR = 10 x weight(kg) + 6.25 x height(cm) - 5 x age + 5
Female: BMR = 10 x weight(kg) + 6.25 x height(cm) - 5 x age - 161
Daily burn = BMR x activity factor (1.2 sedentary to 1.9 very active).
howTo: Select Male or Female and pick metric (cm/kg) or imperial (ft/in, lb).
Enter your age, height and weight honestly.
Choose the activity level that best describes your typical week.
Read your BMR, the extra calories your activity adds, and your total daily burn.
Use the total daily burn as your maintenance-calorie starting point.
keyFacts: BMR is the energy your body burns at complete rest in 24 hours, just to keep you alive.
The Mifflin-St Jeor equation (1990) is the most widely validated BMR formula in clinical use.
Men average a higher BMR than women of the same size, mostly due to more muscle mass.
BMR typically falls 1-2% per decade after age 20 as muscle mass declines.
Activity factors range from 1.2 (sedentary) to 1.9 (very active), multiplying BMR into daily burn.
A 30-year-old man at 70 kg and 175 cm has a BMR of about 1,649 kcal per day.

bmr-calculator.quickAnswer: BMR is the calories your body burns at complete rest. A 30-year-old man weighing 70 kg at 175 cm has a BMR of about 1,649 kcal/day by the Mifflin-St Jeor formula. With moderate exercise 3-5 days a week (factor 1.55), activity adds about 907 kcal, for a total daily burn of roughly 2,556 kcal - your maintenance-calorie starting point.
bmr-calculator.tagline: Find your basal metabolic rate plus activity calories - the starting point for any calorie plan.
bmr-calculator.workedExample:
Male, 30 years, 70 kg, 175 cm, moderate activity:
1. 10 x 70 = 700.
2. 6.25 x 175 = 1,093.75.
3. 5 x 30 = 150; male adds 5.
4. BMR = 700 + 1,093.75 - 150 + 5 = 1,648.75, about 1,649 kcal/day.
5. Moderate activity x1.55: 1,649 x 0.55 = 907 kcal from activity.
6. Total daily burn = 1,649 + 907 = 2,556 kcal/day.
